features.description: Add two-mode recipe suggestions: 'What can I make?' (inventory-first) vs 'I want to make...' (recipe-first). Currently users who type specific recipe requests get ignored because the prompt is inventory-first. Instead of detecting intent, give users an explicit mode toggle.
steps: STEP 1 - UI: In src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/inspire/page.tsx, add a mode toggle at the top of the form with two buttons: 'What can I make?' (inventory mode, default) and 'I want to make...' (recipe mode)

STEP 2 - UI: When mode is 'recipe', hide the ingredient multi-select picker (not needed), show a prominent text input 'What do you want to make?', keep cooking methods filter, hide the remarks textarea (the recipe input IS the main request)
STEP 3 - UI: Store mode in state: const [mode, setMode] = useState<'inventory' | 'recipe'>('inventory')
STEP 4 - API: In src/app/api/suggestions/route.ts, add 'mode' to the request body destructuring and pass it to generateMealSuggestions options

STEP 5 - PROMPT: In src/lib/gemini/vision.ts generateMealSuggestions, add mode to options interface. If mode === 'recipe', use a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT prompt that starts with 'The user wants to make: [remarks]. Help them make this recipe. Here is their inventory:' - the recipe request must be FIRST, inventory SECOND

STEP 6 - PROMPT: For recipe mode, the prompt should: (1) generate the requested recipe as FIRST suggestion, (2) list ingredients they HAVE from inventory, (3) list ingredients they NEED TO BUY, (4) generate alternative similar recipes for remaining slots
STEP 7 - CLEANUP: Remove the fragile hasSpecificRecipeRequest keyword detection (lines ~499-522) - the explicit mode toggle makes it unnecessary

STEP 8 - VERIFY: Test inventory mode still works as before. Test recipe mode with 'bittergourd juice with lemon, ginger, turmeric' - first result should BE that juice with ingredients split into have/need
